plan.analysis: Only evidence is p0001: the uniform block scores exactly 2/3. That is the trivial construction, so any deliberate shape search should be tested. The ratio rewards f*f being flat, which a triangular autoconvolution is not; the likely gains come from reshaping f so its autoconvolution has a less pointed top. I bet on direct numerical maximization of R as the main line, plus two genuinely different shape searches (cosine modes and coarse-to-fine multiscale) to avoid over-committing to one basin. No failed experiment exists yet to avoid repeating.

experiments.hypothesis: Uniform is not a local maximum of R under general block perturbations, so greedy/annealed hill climbing on a moderately fine grid will find a shape with R above 2/3.

plan.analysis: p0004 (0.8578, N=42, smooth unimodal) is the strongest line, and its optimizer was crude: random block hill climbing in 42 dims wastes the budget. Two exploitable facts: (i) R is scale-invariant and its gradient w.r.t. h is computable exactly in O(N²) via convolution adjoints, so projected gradient ascent with backtracking should squeeze real gains at small N; (ii) every attainable g=f*f equals f'*f' for a symmetric f' (F(g)=|F(f)|² is real and symmetric), so restricting to symmetric h halves the search dimension at no loss. Bet: precision (gradient) on p0004, dimension reduction (symmetry), and a coarse global basin search, rather than more random perturbation.

experiments.hypothesis: p0004's shape is near-optimal but its 42 heights were only polished by random block perturbations, which converge slowly; exact-gradient ascent with backtracking and sum-normalization will converge to a sharper local optimum of R at the same N and leave budget to also polish N=64/84 upsamplings.
experiments.change: Keep score(). Replace the hill climb with projected gradient ascent: normalize h so sum(h)=1 each iteration; build padded L=[0,conv(h,h),0]; gradL_j = (2L_j + L_{j-1} + L_{j+1})/3; dq/dh_i = 2*sum_j gradL_j*h_{j-i} (compute as 2*correlate(gradL, h, 'valid')-style convolution), and dm/dh_i = 2*h_{k-i} for k=argmax(padded L) (clip index). Then dR/dh = dq/dh/m - q*dm/dh/m**2, project onto sum-zero (subtract mean), take multiplicative step h *= exp(eta*(h*grad)/ (max|h*grad|+1e-30)) with eta in {1,0.3,0.1} accepted by backtracking on exact score. Loop until 0.85*budget; if 500 iterations pass with <1e-10 gain, perturb h by 2% multiplicative noise around best and continue. After 60% of budget, also upsample best to N=64 and N=84 with np.interp and re-polish each for a share of the remaining time; return the best-scoring array over all N. Print R per restart.
experiments.prediction: R > 0.865 at N=42 (vs 0.8578), with the log showing convergence within a few hundred iterations; the N=64/84 polish either edges higher or plateaus at the same value, indicating p0004 is a genuine local optimum in shape not resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: A coarse global search (only ~5-6 symmetric free parameters, tens of thousands of exact evaluations) can find a different basin than p0004's local climb, specifically a flatter-topped f*f; upsampling and polishing that coarse winner then beats 0.8578. p0006's coarse-to-fine failed only because it started from uniform at N=32 with a weak perturber and never explored randomized coarse shapes.
experiments.change: Write a program that: (1) draws 30000 random coarse vectors c of length 6 with entries exp(N(0,0.7)) times a random Dirichlet(1) weight, mirrors each to a symmetric N=12 array, scores it exactly, and keeps the top 30 (dedupe by shape correlation > 0.99); (2) splits the remaining time equally among those 30: upsample to N=48 with np.interp, then run the exact-gradient ascent from experiment 1 (projected, normalized, backtracking) with a small multiplicative jitter (2%) repeated up to 3 times per seed, keeping the best; (3) uses the final 20% of budget to polish the overall best at N=72 and N=96 the same way. Print the top coarse scores and the final R per N. Do not stop early; keep looping seeds until 0.85*budget.
experiments.prediction: The best coarse shapes will have a noticeably flatter f*f top (larger fraction of knots within 1% of max than p0004's 37.7%); the polished winner reaches R >= 0.865. If it instead plateaus near 0.858, p0004's basin is the right one and only precision (not global search) matters.

experiments.hypothesis: Since F(f*f)=|F(f)|^2 is real and symmetric, replacing f by the symmetric function IFT(|F(f)|) leaves f*f (hence R) unchanged, so a symmetric optimum exists; optimizing only the N/2 free symmetric coordinates halves the dimension and should converge faster/deeper than p0004's unconstrained 42-dim climb in the same budget.
experiments.change: Take p0004 heights, symmetrize (0.5*(h+h[::-1])), interpolate to even N=64. Represent h by v of length N/2 (v[i]=h[i]=h[N-1-i]) and, in every evaluation and update, expand v to length N by mirroring. Run the method of experiment 1 but on v only: use finite-difference? No — use the full gradient dR/dh from the analytic formula, then fold it to v by g_v[i] = g_h[i] + g_h[N-1-i], project to sum-zero, multiplicative backtracking update, v clipped at 1e-12. Do 5 restarts within the budget: first from symmetrized p0004, the rest from random symmetric shapes (cosine bump powers (1+cos)^a with a in [1,6], and top-hat/trapezoid profiles) with jitter, each given an equal time slice; keep the best. Report final N=64 symmetric R and the symmetrized p0004 score for comparison.
experiments.prediction: Symmetric optimization reaches at least p0004's 0.8578 (often 0.862-0.87 at N=64) and converges in noticeably fewer evaluations; if the symmetrized start already scores within 1e-3 of p0004, that confirms the WLOG-symmetry argument and validates half-dimension search as the cheaper route to higher R.

plan.analysis: p0010 (0.8620) is the best and its adaptive hill climb improved p0004 by +0.0042; p0011's coarse symmetric search found a different, flatter-topped basin at 0.8603 but was under-polished. F8 says plain gradient ascent stalls, so gains must come from better exploration or a smarter objective. I bet on three directions: stronger correlated multi-resolution local search around p0010, transplanting p0010's successful hill climb onto p0011's flatter basin, and optimizing a smoothed-max surrogate to directly flatten f*f's top.

experiments.hypothesis: p0010's independent block/single-point perturbations are inefficient; correlated smooth perturbations and subpixel shift/stretch moves can explore the N≈50-90 shape space better and raise R above 0.862.
experiments.change: Keep p0010's score and adaptive hill-climb skeleton, but replace the proposal mix with: (a) with prob 0.5, draw a smooth random field g of length n by taking rng.normal(size=n), convolving with a Gaussian kernel of random width 1-5, normalizing g to unit std, and multiplying heights by exp(sigma*g); (b) with prob 0.25, resample the whole height profile at a subpixel shift delta in [-1,1] and stretch factor in [0.9,1.1]; (c) otherwise use the existing single/block additive moves. Run 4 independent chains initialized by resampling p0010 to N=48, 58, 72, 90, each with its own RNG and 1/4 of the budget, and return the best true-scoring result over all chains.
experiments.prediction: At least one chain improves on 0.8620, reaching R >= 0.864; if all plateau at or below 0.862, the weakness is not the proposal geometry.

experiments.hypothesis: p0011 found an independently flatter f*f top (40.0% of knots within 1% of max) but its gradient polish stalled; applying p0010's proven adaptive stochastic hill climb should combine p0011's better basin with effective exploration.
experiments.change: Take p0011's heights, resample to N=58 with np.interp, and run exactly p0010's adaptive multiplicative/additive/smoothing hill climb (same score, step decay/reset, annealing acceptance, resolution resampling, restarts) from that start for 80% of the budget. Use the remaining 20% to repeatedly resample the current best to N=64/72/84 and continue the same hill climb, keeping the best true R. Use a fresh RNG seed different from p0010's.
experiments.prediction: The transplanted hill climb lifts p0011's 0.8603 to at least 0.862, and possibly above 0.864 if the flatter-top basin is genuinely better than p0010's.

experiments.hypothesis: True R's max term is piecewise constant and creates a jagged landscape; optimizing a smoothed-max surrogate encourages a flatter f*f top and can find shapes that true-R hill climbing misses.
